plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled, ancient-looking branches burst into spicy-sweet, blush-pink blossoms while the landscape is still bare and cold. Ume groves across Japan glow softly in the winter light, and festivals draw crowds to walk beneath the fragrant boughs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, with Japan's ume festivals peaking in February
plants.location: Japan, in plum groves, temple gardens and parks
plants.funFact: Ume flowers open before the leaves appear. In East Asian culture they symbolize perseverance, because they bloom in the cold of late winter.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding white bells with delicate green markings push up through frosty leaf litter and sometimes snow. Snowdrops carpet woodlands and old churchyards in drifts, and they are often the first sign that winter is loosening its grip.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, usually at their peak in February
plants.location: United Kingdom and Europe, in woodlands, churchyards and gardens
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make natural antifreeze-like compounds that help them survive frost. The plant also yields galantamine, a compound developed into a medicine for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere's summer they fill sunny borders and roadsides with bright color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from about December to February in New Zealand
plants.location: New Zealand, where it is widely grown in gardens and on roadsides (native to South Africa)
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily. Agapanthus belongs to the amaryllis family, and its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.
